The Challenge

A restaurant of royal grandeur.
A website of everyday template.

Lal Qila welcomes guests into a Mughal-era fortress of arches, lanterns and waterfalls. Online, the original site carried the crimson but none of the drama: tiny nav dropdowns, identical buttons, a hard-to-read hero and a thin gallery. I kept every real piece of content, and rebuilt the experience around it.

I

Challenge

Make a heritage brand feel as grand online as it does at the table, without inventing anything new.

II

Approach

Same logo, copy, photos and brand red. New structure, dark cinematic canvas, gold accents and 3D depth.

III

Result

A fully interactive site where locations, buffet menus, brands and certifications are one tap away.

Problems → Solutions

What was holding the original back

01

Hidden locations

Karachi, Lahore, Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Johannesburg sat in tiny dropdown items in the nav.

→ A filterable Our Locations section with Order, Buffet Menu and Reservation per branch.
02

Weak hierarchy

Order Online, Buffet Menu and Reservation were three identical red buttons with equal weight.

→ Reservation and Order Online become clear primary actions in the header and hero.
03

Low-contrast hero

A long uppercase tagline over a busy, darkened photo was hard to read.

→ A short, bold headline beside a framed fortress image, on a calm dark ground.
04

Buried menus & brands

Sunday Brunch, Lunch, Hi-Tea and Dinner menus, plus Curry Leaves, LQ Foods, Des Pardes and Catering, were not surfaced.

→ Dedicated Buffet Menu and Our Brands sections, one tap each.
05

Small gallery

Four small tiles in a carousel undersold a spectacular venue.

→ A rich mosaic gallery and dedicated Dining Areas showcase.
06

Sparse trust signals

ISO 9001:2015, UKAS and Halal certifications floated in empty space; testimonials were cramped.

→ Labelled certification cards and a swipeable testimonial carousel.
Design System

Royal red, burnished gold

The original crimson stays as the brand anchor. A deep maroon-black canvas and gold accents bring the warmth of lamp-lit Mughal architecture.

Process

How I approached it

Audit

Reviewed the live site and listed usability and hierarchy problems.

Keep

Preserved the real logo, content, imagery and brand colours.

Restructure

Reorganised content into clear sections: locations, menus, brands, trust.

Elevate

Added a 3D, interactive UI layer and delivered HTML plus an editable Figma file.

Thank you

Lal Qila, ready for its next chapter.
